sections.title: Idioms & phrases
sections.text:
Sweeping Statement – व्र्ापक वतिव्र् Generalised statement He prefers a complicated sentence to a
sweeping statement.
All at sea – उलझन में Puzzled I'm all at sea; I've no idea how to repair
cars.
Enough rope – खुली छुट देना Enough freedom for action They're giving me enough rope to perform
this task.
By fits and start – बीच बीच मेंरूक कि Irregularly He worked on his book by fits and start.
Fell foul of – मुक्ककल मेंफं स जाना Got into trouble with Manufacturers may fall foul of the new
government guidelines.
Token strike – सांके तिक हड़िाल Short strike held as warning They called a 24 hour token strike.
Face the music – ककर्ेका परिणाम भुगिना Get reprimanded You've been caught cheating now you
must face the music.
Look down upon – िुच्छ समझना Hate intensely You shouldn't look down upon him just
because he is poor.
Flogging a dead horse – व्र्र्थयका प्रर्त्न
किना
Wasting time in useless
effort
You're flogging a dead horse by asking him
to lend you money.
Under a cloud – संदेह केघेिेमें Under suspicion The butcher is under a cloud because the
inspectors found that his scales were not
honest.

sections.title: Verbal phrases
sections.text:
Account for
(something) -
To explain the reason for (जबाब देना) You are accounted for your
misdemeanour.
Add up- To join or unite so as to increase in size, quantity,
quality or scope (मेंजुड़ जाना क्जससेमाप/भािि में
बढ़ोत्िि हो जार्े)
Add up these words to your word bank.
Answer for- To be responsible for (जबाबदेह होना)
I am not answerable for this mistake.
Ask after To make inquiries about the health of someone
(ककसी की सेहि के बािेमेंपूछिाछ किना)
I met Alka and she was asking after you.
Ask for (something) To demand (ककसी वस्िुकी मांग किना) She was asking for a hike in her salary.

sections.title: Fixed prepositions
sections.text:
Abound in - (rich in) Uttar Pradesh abounds in water resources.
Abound with (Adj)- (full of) The forest is abound with streams. (teeming with)
Absolve from- (declare free from guilt, promise, duty
etc.)
The court has absolved him from the crime.
Absorb in- (busy in work) He is completely absorbed in his work.
Abstain from- (hold oneself back, used for food habits) His doctor asked him to abstain from drinks.

sections.title: Cloze-test vocabulary
sections.text:
1 Access - पहुंच Approach The only access to the village is by boat.
Accession - पदािोहण Coming to throne 1926 was the year of Emperor Hirohito's accession to the
throne.
Excess - अधधक More than desired An excess of enthusiasm is not always a good thing.

Except - के अलावा Leaving out Everyone was there except for Shivam.
Expect - आशा किना Hope They are expecting a lot of applicants for the job.

sections.title: Verbal phrases
sections.text:
Attend on - To serve (सेवा करना) Radhika has many servants to attend on her.
Back off - To retreat/ to choose not to take action
(दावा छोड़ देना)
Finally, she backed off from her claim on the
property.
Back out - To withdraw from something before
completion/to fail to keep promise (कायमपूरा होनेके
पहलेपीछेहट जाना)
You should not back out from your promise.
Back up - To support (सहायिा देना)
I needed power back up in case the light went
off!
Bank upon/
Count on -
To rely on (ववश्वास करना या तनभमर होना) You cannot bank upon him as he may take you
in at any time.

sections.title: Fixed prepositions
sections.text:
Abstemious in- (eating & drinking) Those who are abstemious in food habits enjoy good health.
Accede to- (a request or proposal) He acceded to my request.
Access to- (means of reaching, approaching) I have no access to the Prime Minister.
Adhere to- (stick to) We decided to adhere to the programme already agreed
upon.
Approve of- (give one's approval) She approved of my proposal in no time.

sections.title: Cloze-test vocabulary
sections.text:

Altar - वेदी place of worship He bowed before the altar.
2 Assent - थवीकृति agree The director has given her assent to the proposals.
Ascent - चढाई climbing up She made her first successful ascent of Everest last year.

sections.title: Idioms & phrases
sections.text:
Going places – प्रवतभाशाली और सफल Talented and successful Here's a guy who really had a chance to
go places.
In cold blood – विदगयतापूिगक हत्या A murder done without intention According to the Red Cross about 220
people were murdered in cold blood.
Off and on – कभी-कभी Occasionally It drizzled off and on all day.
Hard and fast – अपररितगिीय/ विवित Strict Our factory has a hard and fast rule
against smoking.
Took to heels – बहुत ही तेज़ भार्िा शुरू करिा Run away in fear They took to their heels when they saw
the policeman approaching.
To keep up – संपकग मेंरहिा To keep in touch I have kept up with my college mates.

money.

वहचवकचािा

towards the militants.

sections.title: Verbal phrases
sections.text:
Bear down - To overthrow or crush by force
परास्त कर देिा
We have to bear down our enemies.
Bear upon - To be relevant सम्बस्न्धत होिा/प्रासंवर्क होिा Will the new law bear upon the outcome of the case?
Bear out - To support the truth/substantiate सही सावबत
करिेमेंसहायक होिा
This document will bear out your claim on this building.
Bear up - To withstand stress or difficulty सहिा Everyone has to bear up some difficulties.
Bear with - To tolerate with someone बदागश्त करिा Our server is down. Kindly bear with us.

sections.title: Fixed prepositions
sections.text:
Assent to- (official agreement e.g., to a proposal) The President has given assent to the Bill.
Abhorrent of- (abhor, to hate) He is abhorrent of the dowry system.
Acquaint with- (familiar with) I am not acquainted with this lady.
Addicted to- (be given to something harmful) He is addicted to alcohol.
Assured of- (positive about) I am assured of his help in need.

sections.title: Cloze-test vocabulary
sections.text:
1. Adopt- अपिािा/र्ोद लेिा take up They've adopted a baby girl.
Adapt- अिुरूप बिािा adjust The organisms were forced to adapt in order to survive.
Adept- विपुण expert They soon became adept at bartering in the market.
2. Amicable- सौहादगपूणग friendly An amicable settlement was reached.
Amiable- सुशील/ वप्रय lovable, obliging He is a perfectly amiable young man.

sections.title: Idioms & phrases
sections.text:
To stave off – टालना Postpone She brought some fruit on the journey to stave off
hunger.
To give a piece of mind – डांटना To reprimand He stopped making so much noise after I went over
there and gave him a piece of my mind.
Rest on laurels – पुरानी ख्याति पर संिोष तकयेबैठे
रहना
To be complacent Just because you've got your degree doesn't mean
you can rest on your laurels.
Pay through nose – ज्यादा कीर्ि चुकाना Pay an extremely high price We paid through the nose to get the car fixed.
Draw on fancy – कल्पना का प्रयोग करना Use imagination The poet drew on his fancy in his poem.
Turn an honest living – इर्ानदारी सेधन कर्ाना Make a legitimate living He has never turned an honest living in his life.
Give the game away – रहस्य उजागर कर देना Give out the secret It's a secret, so don't give the game away, will you?
Cheek by jowl – घुलतर्लकर/ पास-पास Very near/ close together They lived cheek by jowl in a one-room flat.
Give in – हार र्ान लेना/ पीछेहटना Yield The rebels were forced to give in.
Run riot –बगावि करना/ उपद्रवी होना Act without restraint Rampaging prisoners ran riot through the jail.

sections.title: Verbal phrases
sections.text:
Become of - To happen घतटि होना I wonder what became of my old friends.
Boil down to - To be reduced to its essentials. सार तनकलना Please boil down to the main points of this chapter.
Branch out - To spread फै ल जाना We are going to branch out our business soon.
Break down
(of machinery) -
To stop working कार् करना बंद कर देना The bus broke down on the way so I could not reach the station
on time.
Break down
(of person) -
To lose control (emotionally or mentally)
तहम्मि िो देना
We should not break down in adverse situations.

sections.title: Fixed prepositions
sections.text:
Attain to- (Arrive at a position/post) He attained to this status after hard struggle.
Attraction for- (A thing or person) He has an attraction for her.
Attracted to- (Thing or person) He was attracted to her at first sight.
Avail of- (Take advantage of) She availed herself of this opportunity and got success.
Aloof from- (Keep from) Keep aloof from bad boys.

sections.title: Cloze-test vocabulary
sections.text:

Concede- स्वीकार करना Agree She readily concedes that there is much work still to be done.
2. Alteration- पररविमन Change We will have to make a slight alteration to the plans.
Altercation- वाग्युि/ कहा-सुनी Wordy quarrel According to witnesses, the altercation between the two men
started inside the restaurant.

sections.title: Idioms & phrases
sections.text:

sections.title: Verbal phrases
sections.text:
Break forth - To come to view/to appear suddenly (अचानक
उजागर होना)
Chaos might break forth if the police fail to control the situation.
Break in on - To interrupt a conversation or discussion to
intrude. (खलल डालना)
The conversation between Shiv and Sona was going on when
Rahul broke in on it.
Break into - To enter by force (जबरदस्ती प्रवेश करना) The thief broke into the house.
Break off - To stop suddenly/ to end a relationship. (सहसा
रुक जाना)
He broke off in the middle of his lecture yesterday.
Break out - To start suddenly (disease, war etc.) (अचानक
िै लना)
Dengue has broken out in Delhi.

sections.title: Fixed prepositions
sections.text:
Advance for- (Mature) He is advanced for his years.
Advance by- (Prepone by) The visit of Viru has been advanced by days.
Abide by- (Rules, comply with) You should abide by the rules laid down by the committee.
Accused of- (A crime, charge with) He was accused of theft and convicted.
Acquit of- (Crime, fault) He was acquitted of the crime.

sections.title: Cloze-test vocabulary
sections.text:

2. Affect - प्रभाव डालना (verb ) (to influence, to pretend) Your opinion will not affect my decision.
Effect - प्रभाव Noun The results show a statistically significant effect.

sections.text:

Alight on- (the ground) The birds alighted on the roof of my house.
Alight from- (a bus, car, train) When he alighted from the car, he was welcomed with open arms.

sections.title: Verbal phrases

Bring forward - To present प्रस्तुत किना The judge asked me to bring forward a few facts about the proof

Bring in - To produce, yield or earn पैदा किना Our company will bring in a huge profit this month.

Close in - To encircle closely (िारधोंिरफ सेघेरना) The police personnel closed in on the suspect.

Die out - To get extinct दवलुप्त/खत्म हो जािा Several species died out because of climate change.
Dispose of - To sell off/ to get rid of बेचिा/छु टकारा पािा I want to dispose of these old pieces of furniture.
Do away with - To abolish सर्माप्त कर िेिा We should do away with corruption.
Do without - To manage without दकसी चीज के दबिा कार्म चलािा I cannot do without my staff in my business.

sections.title: Fixed prepositions
sections.text:

Benefit from- (Noun) You should derive benefit from the experience of others.
Compensate for- (give something to make up) He compensated me for the damage to my scooter.
Cure of- (a disease) He is cured of illness after long treatment.

Childish- र्मूखथ silly It's time you gave over such childish behaviour.

sections.title: Verbal phrases
sections.text:
Drag on - To stretch लम्बा खीचना The court cases in India drag on for years.
Drive out - To make someone run away भगा देना Drive out the cattle from the field.
Drop in - To come suddenly अचानक पहंचना Some guests dropped in yesterday.
Dwell on - To keep thinking or talking about or relying on something
वकसी बात के बारेमेंबोलतेया सोचतेरिना या उसी पर वनभवर रिना
It is no use dwelling on your misfortunes.
Eat into - To weaken खोखला करना Corruption is eating into our system.

Comply with- (Act in accordance with) You must comply with the rules laid down by the committee.
Condemn to- (Punishment) The accused was condemned to death.
Congratulate on- (Success) Arnav congratulated his friend on success.
Certain of (Sure of)- Those who work hard should be certain of their success.

sections.title: Verbal phrases

Enter into - To start or get involved in (धकसी धवर्य मेंसक्तम्मधलि हो

Fall apart - To break into pieces (धबर्र ाना) Every part of this movement is falling apart.
Fall back - To retreat (पीछेहट ाना) The invading army was forced to fall back due to continuous

Fall back on - To use as a last resort (आश्रय लेना) I have no one to fall back on.
Fall flat - Fail to produce any effect (कोई प्रभाव न छोड़ना) His advice fell flat on us.

Cope with- (Manage work) My advocate cannot cope with heavy court work.

एक र्ुप्त योजना होना

sections.title: Verbal phrases
sections.text:

Go at- to attack especially with energy
पूरी शक्तक्त के साथ हमला करना

Go back on- To break a promise वादेसेमुकर जाना Why did you go back on your promise?

We should go by the traffic rules.
Go down- To be accepted ववश्वास करना, स्वीकार करना The theory of evolution did not go down well initially.

sections.title: Fixed prepositions
sections.text:
Differ from- (In something) She differs from me both in habits and looks.
Deal in- (Trade in) My friend deals in clothes.
Deal with- (A matter, a person) You must learn how to deal with customers.
Dispense with- (To remove, to do without) You cannot dispense with the use of a fan in summer.
Dispense- (To deal out, distribute) As a judge he dispenses equal justice to all and one.

sections.title: Cloze-test vocabulary
sections.text:

the disease.

employees.

extremely formal way

Ceremonial- उत्सव-संबंधी Of ceremony The queen, in full ceremonial dress, presided over the
ceremony.

sections.title: Idioms & phrases
sections.text:

retreat.

Disgust with- (Person, life) Being spiritual he is disgusted with materials like life.
Disgust at- (An act) Everyone felt disgusted at his jokes.

sections.title: Verbal phrases

sections.title: Verbal phrases
sections.text:

Hold down- To prevent, to limit
र क ा, न र्ंनत्रत कर ा
The militants were held down by the Indian army.

executive.

Hunt down- To pursue successfully by diligent searching and chasing

sections.title: Fixed prepositions
sections.text:

Enlarge on/upon- (Write or say more) I need not enlarge on the problem and waste your time.
Endowed with- (Gifted with) His wife is endowed with both charms and talents.
Enamoured with- (A person) Rosalind was enamoured with Orlando at first sight.

sections.title: Cloze-test vocabulary
sections.text:

2 Council- पररर्द An assembly The decision still has to be ratified by the full council.

Counsellor- सलाहकार Advisor He talked to a counsellor about his marriage difficulties.

sections.text:

sections.title: Verbal phrases
sections.text:
Let out- To allow someone or something to leave a place बाहर
जनकालनेिेना
Who has let the dogs out?
Let up- To slow down, to become less severe कम होना The rain let up as soon as we reached the office.
Lie behind- To be the hidden cause जिपा हुआ कारर् होना Everyone knows what lies behind this cold-blooded murder.
Lie in- Exist in something जकसी चीि मेंहोना Beauty lies in the eyes of the beholder.
Light on- To think/find something unexpectedly
अचानक सूझना
She lighted upon a new way of solving the problem.

sections.title: Fixed prepositions
sections.text:
Hear from- (A person) I have not heard from you for a long time.
Hear of- (Something) I heard of this event in Mumbai and rushed back to Delhi.
Hear by (Post, through communication) I heard by a letter about his uncle's death.
Hard by- (Close to) The college is hard by and I go to college on foot.
Hard up- (Financially tight) He is hard up these days.

sections.title: Cloze-test vocabulary
sections.text:
1 Deference- सम्मान Regards Why do you treat your boss with such a deference?
Difference- अंिर Distinction I can never tell the difference between the twins.
Deferment- टालना Postponement I was granted a deferment on my educational loans.
2 Decent- सभ्य Right and suitable I thought he was a decent person.
Descent- उिार/ कु ल Coming down I made a slow and painful descent down the stairs.
She claims direct descent from Mohammed.
Dissent- मिभेि Disagreement His dissent from his family’s religious beliefs caused a lot of ill-feeling.

sections.title: Idioms & phrases
sections.text:
Give up the ghost- मर जाना, काम
करना बांद कर देना
To die, stop working completely My old car had finally given up the ghost.
Water under the bridge –
जो बीत गया सो बीत गया
Something that happened in the past and
is now forgotten or no longer important
Yes, we did have our disagreements but that's water
under the bridge now.
Stick to guns – बात पर अडेरहना Hold on to original decisions I’ll stick to my guns on this matter. I’m sure I’m right.
Out of hand – र्नयांत्रण के बाहर/
तुरांत
Out of control, at once, immediately His application was rejected out of hand.
Things started to get out of hand.
The salt of the earth – बहुत ही
ईमानदार
Very good and honest/ Kind You can trust her: she’s the salt of the earth.
Chest thumping- डी ांगेमारना The act or practice of boasting There was chest-thumping by House Republicans,
who boasted that they had blocked the Democrats
at nearly every opportunity.
Looking forward to – प्रतीक्षा करना/
आशा करना
To expect something or someone I am looking forward to meeting you.
Pied Piper- नेता के गैर र्जम्मेदाराना
वादे

Get on well – र्मत्रवत सम्बन्ध होना Have a friendly relationship Being a likeable person you get on well with
neighbors and friends.
In a pickle – कर्ठन पररक्तथिर्त में In an embarrassing or awkward situation I hate being in a pickle as it makes me frustrated and
stressed.

sections.title: Verbal phrases
sections.text:
Light up- To brighten/to become cheerful
िमकना/खुश हो जाना
The good news will light up her face.
Live by- Follow manners/means in life
मान्यताओां/र्सिाांतोांको मानना
Man should live by principles.
Live up to- To live or act in accordance with
उम्मीदोांपर खरा उतरना
I couldn't live up to my parents' expectations.
Live with- To put up with, resign oneself सहन करना She cannot live with this tension for a long time.
Live through- To endure, survive बदािश्त करना He lived through the rainy days and this made him strong.

sections.title: Fixed prepositions
sections.text:

Healed of- (A disease, cured of) He is healed of illness after long treatment.
Infer from- (Statement) You cannot infer anything from his statement.
Insight into- (Reality, situation) Wise persons have insight into the reality of life.
Impress upon- (A person, advice) The principal impressed upon the students the need for discipline.

sections.title: Cloze-test vocabulary
sections.text:
1 Desert- रेर्गस्तान Noun (sandy land) They were lost in the desert for nine days.
Desert- छोडना Verb (leave) He deserted his wife and family for another woman.
Dessert- र्मठाई Sweet dish She made a fabulous dessert with alternate layers of chocolate and cream.

Domineer- क्रू रता सेशासन
करना

sections.title: Idioms & phrases
sections.text:
Muddle head- बेवकू फ Stupid The muddle-headed manager is often put over by his
employees.

करना

sections.title: Verbal phrases
sections.text:
Look after- Take care of ध्यान रखना She has five children to look after.

बीतेसमय के तकसी अनुभव या बात के बारेमेंसोचना

Look down on/upon- To regard as inferior नीची तनगाह सेदेखना We should not look down upon the poor.
Look for- To try to find खोजना I am looking for my lost book.
Look forward - To expect with pleasure खुशी के साथ इन्तजार करना I am looking forward to meeting you soon.

sections.title: Fixed prepositions
sections.text:
Wish for- (A thing) I don’t wish for anything in life.
Worthy of- (Praise, note) Your remarks are really worthy of note.
Wanting in- (Lacking in) She is wanting in common sense.
Ward off- (Keep at a distance) Hindus believe in many rituals to ward the evils off
Wary of- (Something, Chary of) We should be wary of strangers.

sections.title: Cloze-test vocabulary
sections.text:

Draught- ठं डी हवा का झोंका Current of wind, quantity of liquid Can you shut the door? There’s a draught here.
2 Defective- दोर्पूर्द, त्रुतटपूर्द Having defect If the goods are defective you should get a full refund.
Deficient- तकसी वस्तुका अभाव
होना
Lacking A diet deficient in vitamin D may cause the disease rickets.

sections.title: Idioms & phrases
sections.text:

sections.title: Verbal phrases
sections.text:
Mess about- To spend time without any purpose or plan
समय गबताना (गबना गकसी गिशेष उद्देश्य के)
They mess about at the park annoying the elderly
people.
Mess (someone) up- To beat/ rough someone पीटना They messed up the tourists and robbed them off their
money.
Mess (something) up- To make something disorderly अस्त-व्यस्त करना They messed up all my belongings while I was away.
Mess up- To make an error िलती करना I messed up a question and hence scored fewer marks.
Mess with- To alter something improperly, to deceive or
confuse someone अस्तव्यस्त कर देना/ धोखा देना
Don’t mess with the sitting arrangement.
Don’t try to mess with me.

Key to- (Success) Hard work is key to success.
Lean on- (Depend on) I had to lean on him in difficulties.

Live on- (Food) He lives entirely on vegetables these days.
Live by- (Livelihood, manner) I have to live by the labour of my own hands.

sections.title: Verbal phrases

Occur to- To come to mind ध्यान मेंआना It suddenly occurred to me that my purse was missing.
Part from- To leave or renounce someone छोड़ देना (व्यखि को) I cannot part from my son.
Part with- To leave or renounce something छोड़ देना (वस्तुको) I cannot part with my books.
Pass away- To die मर जाना He passed away in sleep.
Pay for- To suffer for doing some mistake गलती का हजाषना भरना We have to pay for our sins.

Liable for- (Responsible for) I hold you liable for the murder.
Liable to- (Deserve) He is liable to imprisonment and fine.
Laugh with- (Enjoy with others) It is better to laugh with than to laugh at others.

Stand down- To resign, to withdraw as from a political contest

Point out- (Reveal) I pointed out his errors and he got annoyed with me.
Point at- (Blame) No one can point at his character because he is quite honest.

sections.title: Idioms & phrases
sections.text:
Red rag to a bull- जो नकिी को गुस्सा नदलाये That makes someone very angry Her remarks were like a red rag to a bull.
Stir up a Hornet’s nest – बहुत िारी िमस्याएँ
िड़ी करिा
To create a lot of trouble He always comes home and stirs up a Hornet's
nest when his school day has not gone well.
Grey area- स्पष्टता की कमी Lack of clarity The judgment leaves a large grey area and much
scope for argument.
Average out – िंतुलि बिािा Balance Sometimes I pay, sometimes he pays- it seems to
average out.
Purple heart- बहादुरी Bravery The Military Order of the Purple Heart is a very
worthy cause.
Floored – आश्चयरिनकत या भ्रनमत कर देिा To surprise or confuse I was completely floored by Rob's declaration of
love—I had no idea he felt that way about me!
Give way – हार माि जािा/ ढह जािा Collapse His aching legs gave way, and he almost fell.
Tall tales – डी ंग हांकिा Boasting His tall tales were becoming more unbelievable
each day.
Backseat driver – अििाही िलाह देिेवाला
व्यखि
A person who gives unwanted
advice
Several members of the board of directors have
accused him of being a backseat driver.
At random – नबिा नकिी लक्ष्य के / नबिा िोिे
िमझे/ यादृखिक
Without any aim or target Winners will be drawn at random by computer
on the specified date.

sections.title: Verbal phrases
sections.text:
Tone down To lessen the intensity तीव्रता मेंकमी करिा Tone down your voice. I am not your servant.
Touch upon/on To speak briefly about something
व्याख्या करिा (िंनिप्त)
He did not touch upon the important aspects of socialism
in his speech.
Touch up- To improve by making minor correction
तेजी िेबढ़ािा
The artists touch up their makeup before the camera is
switched on.
Toy with- To play with
नकिी योजिा पर अिमिेढंग िेनविार करिा
You are toying with my dream project.
Try on- To wear something briefly (to check its fit) पहिकर
देििा
I tried on this new dress but it didn't fit me.

sections.title: Fixed prepositions
sections.text:
Pity for (Noun)- We should feel pity for the poor.
Pity on (Noun)- He should take pity on the poor.
Pity (Verb)- We should pity the poor.
Pride on (Verb)- They prided themselves on their wealth.
Pride in (Noun)- They take pride in their wealth.

sections.title: Cloze-test vocabulary
sections.text:
1 Gamble- जुआ िेलिा To play for stake I gambled all my winnings on the last race.
Gambol- उछल कू द करिा To frisk Lambs were gambolling around in the spring sunshine.
2 Graceful- िुंदर Beautiful She was slim and extremely graceful.
Gracious- दयालु Kind, merciful Lady Caroline was gracious enough to accept our invitation.

sections.title: Idioms & phrases
sections.text:
In the limelight-प्रर्धान Prominent She likes being in the limelight.
Go haywire – सब अस्त - व्यस्त होना
/ अटनयंटित हो जाना
Become wildly confused,
out of control, or crazy
Everything would go haywire if he saw her.
To be in brown study- ख्यालोंमें
खोयेरहना
Be lost in imagination I could see she was in a brown study.
Feather in one’s cap – उपलब्धि An achievement Shobhit's appointment to this important post was a feather in his
cap.
Follow one’s nose – नाक की सीर्ध
मेंचलना/ सीर्धी रेखा मेंचलना
To go straight ahead Turn left, then just follow your nose and you’ll see the shop on
your left.
Sail under false colours- पाखंडी A hypocrite I don't want to be accused of sailing under false colours, so let
me say that I'm being paid to give a review of this product today.
Fight shy of – बचना/ दू र रहना To avoid someone/
something
Before this course I’d always fought shy of technology.
Wear the green willow – प्यार का
उत्तर न टमलनेसेदुखी हो जाना
To grieve for lost or
unrequited love
My grandmother has been wearing the green willow ever since
my grandfather died.
Cock and bull story – मनगढ़ंत
कहानी
Absurd and unbelievable
story
She started to tell some cock and bull story to the police officers
about how she found a huge bag containing 5 pounds of gold.
Hold water – टवश्वास यो ग्य होना Seem logical The jury convicted her because her story just didn't hold water.

sections.title: Verbal phrases
sections.text:
Turn down To refuse or reject अस्वीकार कर देना (अनुरोर्ध आटद) He turned down my offer.
Turn out (to be) To prove to be साटबत होना He turned out to be a crook.
Turn out To come to a meeting or to form a crowd टकसी मीटिंग में
उपब्धस्थत होना / भीड़ के रूप मेंइकठ्ठा होना
Many party workers turned out for the rally.
Turn up To arrive टकसी कायवक्रम मेंशाटमल होना Students turned up for the test.
Wait on To serve the needs of, visit सेवा करना The hosts waited on the guests.

sections.title: Fixed prepositions
sections.text:
Proud of We should be proud of our country.
Prompt in- (Quick in) You should be prompt in doing your duty.
Quick at- (A thing) The dog is quick at smelling.
Quick in- (Doing a thing) The boy is quick in working out the problems.
Quick of- (Understanding) The child is very quick of understanding.

sections.title: Cloze-test vocabulary
sections.text:
1 Gate- द्वार Door He pushed open the garden gate.
Gait-चलनेका ढंग A way of walking or running He walked with an awkward gait like a penguin.
2 Gravitation- आकर्वण-शब्धि Pulling towards, attracting Particles are attracted to each other by gravitation.
Gravity- गंभीरता Quality of being serious I don’t think you understand the gravity of the situation.

sections.title: Idioms & phrases
sections.text:
To be down to earth – व्यावहाररक To be realistic Santy is a very friendly, down to earth person.
In the nick of time – ठीक सर्मय पर Just in time We made it to the airport in the nick of time to catch our
flight.
To shun evil company – बुरी संगनत छोड़
देना
To avoid or give up bad company He was advised to shun evil company.
Seamy side – अनिय और अनैनतक Unpleasant and immoral The seamy side of life includes crime and other evils.
A sacred cow – नजसकी आलोचना न की
जा सके/ पनवत्रम्मान्य
A person never to be criticised The judiciary remains a sacred cow, despite increasing
evidence that serious mistakes have been made.
A dog’s breakfast – पूरी तरह गड़बड़ /
कार्म जो ढंग सेन नकया गया हो
A total mess / A thing that has
been done badly
They have made a real dog’s breakfast on that display.
Knuckle sandwich- र्मुक्का A punch There were times I wanted to give him a knuckle
sandwich.
Take the bull by the horns –
साहसपूवभक र्मुसीबतोंका सार्मना करना
To face a difficulty courageously I took the bull by the horns and confronted him about his
mistreatment of the workers.
Banana republic- कर्मजोर और भ्रष्ट देश Weak or corrupt country The Agency had huge collections of intelligence on
banana republics and their leaders.
To be in a quandary – उलझन र्में In a confusing situation I've had two job offers, and I'm in a real quandary
about/over which one to accept.

sections.text:

Barn (कमरा धिसमेंफ़सल

है)

Drove (पशुआधि क एक
धवशेष धिशा मेंहााँकना)
A large building with an extensive
floor area, typically for housing
aircraft
Hangar(धवमानशाला)
A crowd or large group of people Throng (ल ग ं की भारी
भीड)
A large bedroom for a number of
people in a school or institution
Dormitory (शयनागार)
A self-governing country or region Autonomy (स्वशासन) A place where babies and young
children are taken care of while
their parents are working, studying,
shopping, etc
Creche (माता-धपता की
अनुपस्स्िधत मेंधशशुओं की
िेखभाल का स्िान)
A place where coins, medals or
tokens are made
Mint (टकसाल ) That which cannot be guessed or
calculated
Imponderable
(अस चनीय)
One who does not take any
alcoholic drink
Teetotaller (कभी भी
मधिरापान न करने वाला
व्यस्ि)
Driving force Impulse (प्र त्साहन)
A person who uses astrology to tell
people about their character, about
what might happen to them in the
future, etc
Astrologer (ज्य धतषी) A place in a large institution, for the
care of those who are ill
Infirmary
(धचधकत्साशाला)
A person who is trained to travel in
a spacecraft
Astronaut (अंतररक्ष यात्री) Having no boundaries or limits Infinite
(अंतहीन, अपररधमत)

sections.title: Idioms & phrases
sections.text:
Cloak and dagger- गुप्त An activity that involves mystery
and secrecy
She was released from prison in a cloak-and-dagger
operation yesterday.
Palm off- ि खा िेना, िु टकारा पाना To dispose off with the intent to
deceive
Jai was palmed off with a series of excuses.
From stem to stern-एक धसरेसेिू सरेधसरे
तक
All the way from the front of a
ship to the back
The ship was in a blaze from stem to stern.
Over egg the pudding – सुिारनेके धलए
अनावश्यक चीि ंक ि डकर और बुरा बना
िेना
To spoil something by trying too
hard to improve it
You can buy all sorts of extras for the car, but it's very easy
to over-egg the pudding.
Turn over a new leaf - नया िीवन शुरू
करना, अच्छेके धलए अपना स्वभाव बिलना
Change one’s behaviour for the
better
She promises to turn over a new leaf if we give her one
more chance.
Take up the hatchet- युद्ध के धलए िाना
या तैयारी करना
Prepare for or go to war He induced the tribes to take up the hatchet against the
English.
At loose ends- धबना कु ि काम के,
अधनधित स्स्िधत में
In an uncertain situation, not
knowing what to do
Adolescents are most likely to get into trouble when
they’re at a loose end.
With might and main- पूरेज र से With full force Everybody rowed with might and main and soon we got
into the safe waters.
Ruffle somebody’s feather- तंग करना Annoy somebody Every single time you drink too much you ruffle
someone's feathers.
Cut short- बािा डालना, समय के पहले
अंत कर िेना
Interrupt, to end (something)
earlier than expected
Their conversation was cut short by the arrival of more
guests.

sections.title: Word series
sections.text:
PATHETIC –
ियनीय
Someone or something that causes
pity - PITIFUL
Syno- miserable, wretched, tragic,
dismal, desolate, mournful, abject
Anto- hilarious, facetious,
whimsical, jocular, gleeful, ecstatic,
hopeful
ACKNOWLEDGEMENT –
स्वीकृ धत
Acceptance of the truth or existence of
something; recognition of the
importance or quality of something -
CONFIRMATION
Syno- admission, acceptance,
confession, cognizance, citation
Anto- ungratefulness, thankless,
denunciation, disregard
IMPLORE –
प्रािथना करना
Act of begging someone
desperately to do something -
PLEAD
Syno- entreat, beseech, petition,
solicit, besiege, grovel
Anto- disapprove, avoid, dissuade,
thwart
PRODIGAL – खचीला Spending money or using resources
freely and recklessly; wastefully
extravagant - EXTRAVAGANT
Syno- luxurious, lavish, opulent,
profligate, sumptuous
Anto- thrifty, economical, frugal,
parsimonious, scrimping
GLORIOUS –
तेिस्वी
Something that is amazing and
admirable - SPLENDID
SOLITARY – अके ला Done or existing alone - SINGULAR
Syno- grand, magnificent,
majestic, grandiose, marvellous,
rapturous
Anto- average, ordinary, mediocre,
pathetic, horrendous, dreadful,
deplorable
Syno- isolated, unique, reclusive,
hermitic, introverted
Anto- accompanied, synchronised,
cordial, gregarious, genial
REVERE –
सम्मान
Feel deep respect or admiration for
(something) - RESPECT
Syno- esteem, honour, venerate,
commemorate
Anto- scorn, abhor, condemn,
deride, contempt, ridicule, mock
FURY – क्र ि Wild or violent anger - ANGER
Syno- ferocity, violence, fierceness,
frenzy, rage, uproar
Anto- mildness, hush, serenity,
tranquility, indifference
PREVENT –
र कना
Keep (something) from happening
- AVERT
Syno- halt, thwart, obviate,
interrupt, embargo, curb, subdue
Anto- initiate, instigate, elicit,
trigger, catalyze
EXPENSIVE –
बहुमूल्य
Costing a lot of money - DEAR
Syno- costly, exorbitant, extortionate,
gaudy, flamboyant, premium
Anto- cheap, affordable, inexpensive,
worthless

sections.title: One-word substitutions
sections.text:
One who studies the occult
meanings of numbers and their
supposed influence on human life
Numerologist
(अंकशास्त्री)
A person who thinks that bad things
are more likely to happen or who
emphasises the bad part of a situation
Pessimist (निराशावादी)
A sentimental longing for a period
in the past
Nostalgia (भूतकाल की
नकसी अवनि की याद)
A dynamic campaign for political, social
or religious change
Crusade (िर्मयुद्ध)
Soft, inner part of a nut or fruit￾stone
Pulp (गूदा) An imaginary ideal society free of
poverty and suffering
Utopia
(आदशम-लोक, रार्राज्य)
The inner part of a nut or seed Kernel (नगरी या बीज का
अंदरूिी निस्सा )
A place or condition of great happiness
where everything is exactly as you
would like it to be
Paradise
(स्वगम, आिंद िार्)
Burnt sugar that is used to add
flavour and colour to food
Caramel
(जली हुई शक्कर भोजि र्ें
रंग और स्वाद के नलए)
One who does not believe in the
existence of God
Atheist (िास्तिक)
A news article that reports the
recent death of a person
Obituary (शोक-सर्ाचार) An arrangement of flowers that is
usually given as a present
Bouquet (गुलदस्ता)
Something that is to your
advantage but happened by
chance
Fortuitous
(आकस्तिक लाभ)
A small shop that sells fashionable
clothes or expensive presents
Boutique
(छोटी दुकाि जिााँलोकनिय
कपड़े या र्िाँगे उपिार
नबकतेिैं)
To prevent something, especially a
system, process, or event, from
continuing as usual or as expected
Disrupt (नवघ्ि पैदा करिा,
नवघटि करिा)
One who supervises in an examination
hall
Invigilator (निरीक्षक)
To explode, or to make a bomb or
other device explode
Detonate(नवस्फोट करिा) A person preoccupied with an
unrealistically optimistic approach to
life
Quixotic (अव्याविाररक)
The act or habit of talking in one's
sleep
Somniloquy
(सोतेसर्य बात करिा)
The crime of attacking somebody
physically
Battery (शारीररक िर्ला
करिेका अपराि)

sections.title: Idioms & phrases
sections.text:
Bad blood- र्िर्ुटाव, कटुता Ill feeling There is bad blood between them.
A laughing stock- िंसी का पात्र An object of laughter His constant blunders made him the laughing stock of the
whole class.
To keep the wolf from the
door- नकसी तरि सेगुजारा करिा
Avoid starvation As a student, he took an evening job to keep the wolf
from the door.
Teething problems- िारस्तिक
कनििाइयााँ
Problems at the start of a new
project
There were some teething problems when we began our
business.
Mealy-mouthed-र्ृदुभाषी, ख़ुशार्दी Afraid to speak frankly or
straightforwardly
Spokesmen have been mealy-mouthed in defence of the
president.
By fits and starts- अनियनर्त रूप से,
कभी कभी
Irregularly If you work by fits and starts, you will never achieve much.
Rat race – गलाकाट िनतयोनगता A way of life in which people are
caught up in a fiercely competitive
struggle for wealth or power
Dad wants to get out of the rat race and move to the
countryside.
Spin one's wheels- सर्य या र्ेिित
बबामद करिा
Expel much effort or time for little or
no gain
So for at least five of the last eight years, I was just
spinning my wheels.
The alpha and the omega- आनद
औैर अंत, प्यार और िफरत, र्ुख्य भाग
The love and the hatred, most
important part
He knows the alpha and omega of his job.
Throw up the sponge- आत्मसर्पमण
करिा
To surrender I would throw up the sponge and walk out.

sections.title: Word series
sections.text:

बिाए रखिा

- MAINTAIN
Syno- preserve, hold, withhold,
grasp, recruit, secure
Anto- relinquish, lose, yield,
abdicate, renounce, sack
OVATION -
स्वागत, अनभिंदि
Sustained show of appreciation through
applause- APPLAUSE
Syno- cheering, plaudits, accolade,
laurels, laudation, salutation,
Anto- contempt, mockery, scorn, sarcasm,
burlesque, banter
ERUDITE –
नवद्वाि
Having or showing great knowledge
or learning - LEARNED
Syno- cheering, plaudits, accolade,
laurels, laudation, salutation,
Anto- contempt, mockery, scorn,
sarcasm, burlesque, banter
PREFERRED –
पसंदीदा
Someone who is recommended￾FAVOURED
Syno- endorsed, selected, approved,
desired , elect,
Anto- unfavored, rejected, abhorred,
loathed, despised
VIOLENT –
निंसक
Using or involving physical force
intended to hurt, damage, or kill
someone or something -
AGGRESSIVE
DISHEARTENED –
निराश
Having lost determination or confidence;
dispirited - DEPRESSED
Syno- dejected, despondent, daunted,
jaded, flustered, agitated
Syno- brutal, frenzied, callous,
ruthless, barbaric, frantic
Anto- peaceful, benign, virtuous,
moderate, endurable
Anto- gleeful, jubilant, blissful, exuberant,
rapt
CATASTROPHIC -
आपनिजिक
Something that involves sudden and
large damage - DISASTROUS
Syno- unfortunate, direful,
detrimental, fatal, grievous
Anto- advantageous, beneficial,
auspicious, fortuitous
CORDIAL -
सौिादमपूणम
Warm and friendly; strongly felt - AFFABLE
Syno- unfortunate, direful, detrimental,
fatal, grievous
Anto- advantageous, beneficial,
auspicious, fortuitous
DEFICIENCY –
कर्ी
Lack of something- INADEQUACY
Syno- shortage, scantiness, paucity,
shortfall, insufficiency
Anto- abundance, surplus, plethora,
surfeit, ampleness
REPERCUSSION –
िनतनिया, िभाव
An unintended consequence of an event
or action - REACTION
Syno- consequence, corollary, aftermath,
resultant, outcome
Anto- cause, origin, commencement,
precursor, anticlimax

sections.title: One-word substitutions
sections.text:
A person appointed by two parties
to solve a dispute
Arbitrator (पञ्च) To be deeply asleep Slumber(गहरी नी ींद सोना)
The number of deaths in one period
of time or in one place
Mortality
(मृत्यु-सींख्या, मृत्युदर)
An examination of a dead body to
determine the cause of death
Post-mortem
(मृत्युका कारण जाननेके लिए
डॉक्टरी शव-परीक्षा)
A musical composition made up of
a series of songs or short pieces
Medley
(स्वर-लमश्रण, गीत-लमश्रण)
A person who presents a
radio/television programme
Anchor (उद् घोषक)
A person who entertains people by
doing difficult feats
Acrobat (किाबाजी) The art of effective or persuasive
speaking or writing
Rhetoric (वाक्पटुता)
A secret or disguised way of writing Cypher (गुप्त लिलप) Old and no longer used Archaic (प्राचीन)
An object or symbol that represents
something
Emblem
(प्रतीक वस्तुया लचह्न)
A person employed to drive a
private or hired car
Chauffeur (मोटर-चािक)
Urge or force (a person) to do an
action
Impel (उत्तेजना करना) To pretend to be somebody else in
order to trick people or to
entertain them
Impersonate
(अलिनय करना)
A mixture of loud unpleasant
sounds
Cacophony
(ऊँ चेअलप्रय स्वर, बेसुरापन)
A place where somebody lives Abode (लनवास)
A corporation made up of a number
of different companies that operate
in diversified fields
Conglomerate
(लवलिन्न कीं पलनयोीं सेलमिकर
बनी एक बड़ी कीं पनी)
Having no definite form or distinct
shape
Amorphous (अनाकार)
A short rest or sleep taken after
lunch
Siesta (दोपहर का आराम) Having a mental age of three to
seven years
Imbecile (मूर्ख)

sections.title: Idioms & phrases
sections.text:
To put a spoke in one's wheel- काम
लबगाड़ना
To put a difficulty in the way of
progress
It will really put a spoke in our wheel if the board decides
not to increase our funding for this project.
At loggerheads- असहमत, अनबन In conflict with someone Management and staff are at loggerheads over the plan.
A wild goose chase- लनरर्खक र्ोज Useless search Avgat looking for his lost phone may be on a wild goose
chase.
A moot point- लववाद का लवषय Disputed Whether he was serious is a moot point.
Spick and Span- साफ़ - सुर्रा Neat and clean They always keep their kitchen spick and span.
To draw the longbow- बढ़ा-चढ़ाकर
कहना
To exaggerate We cannot believe him because he used to draw the long
bow.
All agog- प्रिालवत या आश्चयखलकत Amazed or impressed He sat there, all agog, as the master of ceremonies read
his name as the winner of first prize.
Not to mince matters- मुींह पर कहना To speak frankly Not to mince matters, I don’t approve of my daughter
going out with you because you are a married man.
Kick the bucket- मर जाना To die Every one of us will kick the bucket someday.
An axe to grind- अपना मतिब होना To have a selfish motive Whenever he flatters your generosity, he will certainly
have an axe to grind.

sections.title: Word series
sections.text:
JUVENILE - लकशोर Relating to young people - CHILDISH
Syno- infantile, adolescent, chap,
jejune, puerile, fatuous
Anto- elderly, mature, sophisticated,
adult, veteran
ASSAULT –
हमिा करना
Make a physical attack on someone or
something - ATTACK
Syno- strike, onslaught, affray, raid, assail,
plunder
Anto- defence, resistance, shielding, guard
SACRED - पलवत्र Connected with God or a god or
dedicated to a religious purpose and
so deserving veneration —HOLY
Syno- divine, heavenly, supernatural,
mystic, pious, sacramental
Anto- sinful, impious, profane, vile,
blasphemous
THRIVE –
फिना-फू िना
(Of a child, animal, or plant) grow or develop
well or vigorously; prosper - FLOURISH
Syno- blossom, grow, burgeon, prosper
Anto- decline, retrogress, wither,
degenerate, recede, abate
WEARY –
सुस्त, र्का हुआ
Feeling or showing extreme tiredness,
especially as a result of excessive
exertion - EXHAUSTED
Syno- tired, drained, fatigued, jaded
Anto- rapt, energetic, intrigued,
enthralled
SOLEMN - गींिीर Formal and dignified; characterized by deep
sincerity - SERIOUS
Syno- earnest, sober, profound, glum,
gloomy, grim
Anto- flippant, frivolous, facetious,
bantering, comical
AFFLUENT –
धनी
Having a great deal of money; wealthy
- PROSPEROUS
Syno- opulent, privileged, elite,
fortunate, bountiful
ERADICATE –
उन्मूिन करना
Destroy completely; put an end to; get rid of;
eliminate - UPROOT
Syno- erase, efface, decimate, annihilate,
obliterate
Anto- indigent, penurious, insolvent,
bankrupt, destitute
Anto- save, establish, institute, animate
ACCURATE –
शुद्ध
(Especially of information,
measurements, or predictions) correct
in all details; exact - PRECISE
Syno- veracious, scrupulous,
meticulous, authentic, factual
Anto- inaccurate, imprecise, flawed,
erroneous, vague
ABORT –
बीच मेंबींद करना
Bring to a premature end because of a
problem or fault - END
Syno- halt, terminate, call off, repeal,
revoke, desist, suspend
Anto- continue, sanction, validate, enforce,
approve

sections.title: Idioms & phrases
sections.text:
To go through fire and water-
(कु छ पानेकेलिए बहुत कलिनाइय ोंया खतर ों
सेगुज़रना)
To experience many dangers in
order to achieve something
They were always ready to go through fire and water for
the sake of the friends.
Chicken-hearted- (कायर, डरप क) Coward These chicken-hearted bosses always seem to give in at
the first sign of a strike.
Red letter day- (एक महत्वपूर्णलिन) Significant day June 2nd will be a red-letter day for him, he 's getting
married.
Ended in a fiasco- (पूर्णतः असफि ह ना) A complete failure The meeting ended in a fiasco as the members could not
arrive at a consensus.
Sow wild oats- (ऐय्याशी करना) To waste time by doing foolish
things, to have many sexual
relationships
He sowed all his wild oats before he married.
Live from hand to mouth- (लकसी प्रकार
गुजारा करना)
To have enough money to live on
and nothing extra
My father earned very little and there were four kids, so
we lived from hand to mouth.
To face the music- (लकयेका पररर्ाम
भुगतना)
To bear the consequences Riya broke a dining-room window and had to face the
music when her father got home.
Pillar to post- (मारा मारा लफरना, एक
जगह सेिू सरेजगह)
One place to another She was driven from pillar to post and each person she
spoke to was more unhelpful than the last.
Hobson's choice- (एक ही रास्ता या
लिकल्प)
No real choice at all It's a case of Hobson's choice, because if I don't agree to
their terms, I'll lose my job.
Adam's ale- (पानी) Water If the kids feel tired, let them have a glass of Adam’s ale
from the tap.
At one's wit's end- (हैरान, उिझन में
ह ना)
To get puzzled I’ve tried to do my math homework for more than three
hours and now I’m at my wit’s end.
To steal a march- (आगेलनकिना) To outshine Our rival company managed to steal a march on us by
bringing out their software ahead of ours.
In a jiffy- (पिक झपकतेही) Something that is done very
quickly
Don't worry, boss, I'll have this report typed up in a jiffy!
Herculean task- (कलिन कायण) Very difficult task Painting a kitchen is a Herculean task.
On tenterhooks- (िुलिधा में, बेचैन ह ना) In anxious suspense We were kept on tenterhooks for hours while the judges
chose the winner.
The thin end of the wedge- (लकसी
अलप्रय स्थिलत की शुरुआत)
Start of harmful development Workers believe the job cuts are just the thin end of the
wedge.
To accept the gauntlet- (चुनौती स्वीकार
करना)
To accept challenge The time has come for Congress to accept the gauntlet
and do something about this problem.
To wrangle over an ass' shadow-
(छ टी छ टी बात ोंपर िड़ाई झगडा करना)
To quarrel over trifles Only foolish people wrangle over an ass’ shadow.
Make one's flesh creep- (भयभीत कर
िेना)
To frighten someone The memory of all that blood was enough to make my
flesh creep.
Damp squib- (ऊँ ची िुकान फीका
पकिान)
Complete failure, Someone or
something that disappoints or
does not meet expectations.
They promised us fireworks, but have produced a damp
squib.
Rise like a phoenix- पूरी तरह असफि
ह नेके बाि लफर सेसफि ह ना
To become successful again The country has risen like a phoenix from the ashes of
this devastating civil war.

sections.title: Word series
sections.text:
EXCEED –
अलधक ह ना
Be greater in number or size than
(a quantity, number, or other
measurable thing) - SURPASS
Syno- transcend, outdo, surmount,
subdue, defeat, outnumber
Anto- waive, paucity
PHILANTHROPIST –
जनलहतैषी
Person who seeks to promote the welfare
of others- HUMANIST
Syno- benefactors, patrons, altruists,
partisans
Anto- misanthropists, uncharitable,
malevolent, selfish
RELIEF –
राहत, सहायता
A feeling of happiness that
something unpleasant has not
happened or has ended - AID
Syno- release, discharge,
emancipation, exemption, escape
Anto- concern, anxiety, distress,
unease, dread, panic
STOICAL –
उिासीन
Enduring pain and hardship without
showing one’s feelings or complaining -
APATHETIC
Syno- patient, passionless, calm,
phlegmatic, stolid
Anto- fervid, passionate, vehement,
zealous, ardent, animated
INCLEMENT– कि र,
लनिणयी
(Of the weather) unpleasantly cold
or wet or stormy - STORMY
Syno- rough, severe, harsh, windy,
boisterous, drizzly
Anto- clement, halcyon, calm,
pleasant
OPTIMISTIC –
आशािािी
Hopeful and confident about the future -
BUOYANT
Syno- favourable, utopian, propitious,
upbeat, asupicious
Anto- depressed, hopeless, adverse,
sullen, ominous
LACKADAISICAL –
भािुक
Lacking enthusiasm and
determination - APATHETIC
PREDECESSOR –
पूिणज
A person who held a job or office before
the current holder - ANCESTOR
Syno- indifferent, apathetic,
lethargic, sluggish, slothful,
languid
Anto- ambitious, excited, spirited,
lively, fervent, ebullient
Syno- antecedent, prototype, precursor,
forerunner
Anto- successor, replacement,
descendant, follower
IMPOVERISHED –
िररद्र बना िेना
Made poor—PENNILESS
Syno- destitute, penurious,
indigent, beggarly, famished
Anto- affluent, privileged,
fortunate, plethoric, fraught
PERSIST – दृढ़ रहना To continue to do something despite
difficulties or opposition - PERSEVERE
Syn- abide, endure, obtain, remain

sections.title: Idioms & phrases
sections.text:
Bear the palm- (विजयी होना) To win I heard that you might bear the palm at the science fair.
To give the devil his due- (बुरेव्यक्ति
को श्रेय देना या उसकी प्रशंसा करना)
To give credit to even a notorious
person
I don’t like the man but – give the devil his due – he works
incredibly hard.
To have a finger in every pie- (सब में
फं सा होना)
To be involved in a large and
varied number of activities or
enterprises
When they nominated me for the board, I'm sure Bill had
a finger in the pie.
To make up one's mind- (वनश्चय करना) To make a decision; decide He's thinking about going, but he still hasn't made up his
mind.
To have bitten off more than you can
chew- (अपनी क्षमता सेअविक काययकरने
का प्रयास करना)
To have tried to do something
which is too difficult
I am sure she is biting off more than she can chew by
promising to solve the difficult task in a few minutes that
I couldn’t since the last three days.
Out of print- (प्रकाशक के पास उपलब्ध न
होना )
A book no longer available from
the publisher
Most of her books went out of print years ago.
To hit the nail on the head - (वबल्कु ल
सही जिाब वमलना)
To find exactly the right answer You hit the nail on the head with your proposal at the staff
meeting yesterday.
On thin ice- (जोक्तिम में) In a precarious or risky situation His firm is just on thin ice of bankruptcy.
To heave a sigh of relief- (ठं डी सांस
लेना, जान मेंजान आना)
To suddenly feel very happy
because something unpleasant
has not happened or has ended
They pulled up to the hospital and Jimmy heaved a sigh
of relief.
To be on cloud nine- (बहुत ज्यादा िुश
होना)
To extremely happy He was on cloud nine after winning the competition.
To have something on the brain-
(सनक आना, वदमाग मेंकु छ होना)
To be obsessed with something I have got that song on the brain today.
Not one's cup of tea- (काययजो करना
पसंद ना हो)
Not one's choice or preference Hiking is not my cup of tea, but my husband enjoys it.
In bad taste- (उपयुि न होना) Not suitable or offensive She acknowledged her remark had been in bad taste.
Once and for all- (हमेशा केवलये, आक्तिरी
बार)
Now and for the last time; finally, He came to help her, to appease his guilt once and for all.
To have at one's fingertips- (जानकारी
होना)
Recall of factual information at
one's command
He keeps all facts regarding the sales of the product at his
fingertips.
To not have a clue (कु छ पता न होना) To not know about something I don't have a clue what will happen now.
In black and white- (वलक्तित रुप में) A clear choice that causes no
confusion
He'd seen the proof in black and white.
Out of date- (अप्रचवलत, पुराना;) Old-fashioned His editions of the classics are now, of course, out of date.
It goes without saying – (स्पष्ट होना) Something which is implied to be
obvious
Of course, it goes without saying that you'll be paid for
the extra hours you work.
To let someone off –
(दोष सेमुि करना)
To release someone from blame I’ll let you off this time, but don’t ever lie to me again.

sections.title: Word series
sections.text:
EMPATHY –
सहानुभूवत
The ability to understand another
person’s feelings, experience￾WARMTH
Syn- affinity, compassion, rapport,
cognizance
Ant- disinterest, insouciance,
callousness, dismissiveness
ONEROUS –
कष्टदायक
Needing great effort; causing trouble or
worry - ARDUOUS
Syn- strenuous, gruelling, exhausting,
demanding
Ant- effortless, trifling, temperate,
unchallenging
TURBULENT￾उपद्रिी
Violently disturbed or annoyed -
RAGING
Syn- violent, stormy, ferocious,
blustering
Ant- tranquil, serene, quiet, unruffled
ANIMOSITY –
दुश्मनी
A strong feeling of opposition, anger or hate
- ANTAGONISM
Syn- hostility, bitterness, antipathy, malice
Ant- amity, rapport, benevolence, amiability
COGENT –
ठोस, यकीनी
Strongly and clearly expressed in a
way that influences what people
believe – CONVINCING
Syn- persuasive, rational, valid,
credible
Ant- pointless, lame, impotent, futile
PIQUANT -
तीिा
Having a pleasantly strong or spicy taste -
PUNGENT
Syn- savoury, spiced, zesty, peppery, tangy
Ant- zestless, mild, insipid, flavorless,
distasteful
EVIDENCE￾सबूत
The facts, signs or objects that make
you believe that something is true -
INDICATION
Syn- attestation, verification,
validation, authentication
Ant- refutation, negation, rebuttal,
debunking
MERCURIAL –
अक्तथिर
Often changing - VOLATILE
Syn- capricious, unpredictable, vacillating,
wavering
Ant- steady, predictable, consistent, stable
ALLURING –
मनोहर
Attractive and exciting in a mysterious
way - CHARMING
Syn- enchanting, appealing,
captivating, luring
Ant- repulsive, nauseating, abhorrent,
heinous
DIMINUTIVE –
अल्प
Extremely or unusually small – PETITE
Syn- miniature, minuscule, midget, compact
Ant- mammoth, gigantic, grand, enormous

sections.title: Idioms & phrases
sections.text:
Barking up the wrong tree – (गलत
जगह विचार करना )
Looking in the wrong place His attorney suggested that the investigators might be
barking up the wrong tree.
Call it a day - (कार्यखत्म करना) To declare the end of a task I'm getting a bit tired now - let's call it a day.
Ball is in your court - (आपका दावर्त्व
होना)
It is up to you to make the next
decision or step
I've done all I can; now the ball's in your court.
Best of both worlds – (सिोत्तम स्थिवत) A situation wherein someone has
the privilege of enjoying two
different opportunities
She works in the city and lives in the country, so she gets
the best of both worlds.
Give somebody a ring – (वकसी को फोन
करना)
Call someone on the telephone I'll give you a ring tomorrow.
Leave no stone unturned – (हर संभि
प्रर्ास करना)
Try every possible course of
action in order to achieve
something
The researchers left no stone unturned in their search for
the original documents.
Get the message
(समझना जो सीधेन कहा गर्ा हो)
Understand what is implied by a
remark or action
He gave her an angry look, hoping she'd get the message.
Keep at bay (दू र रखना) To control something and
prevent it from causing you
problems
He held the police at bay for several hours
To go off the air (प्रसारण बंद करना) To stop broadcasting a radio or
TV program
It was my favourite show, but it went off the air last year.
To make a fuss about (बढ़ा चढ़ा कर
बताना)
An excessive display of attention
or activity
If you ask me, they make too much fuss of him.
To go to somebody's head- सर चकरा
देना
To make someone dizzy or
slightly drunk
If alcohol goes to your head, it makes you feel slightly
drunk.
To make amends - प्रार्वित करना To compensate He wanted to make amends for causing their marriage to
fail.
Get on the nerves - परेशान होना To be an irritant Stop laughing! You are getting on my nerves.
Keep under one's hat - कु छ गुप्त रखना To keep something a secret I'll only tell you if you promise to keep it under your hat.
Go for a song - अप्रत्यावशत रूप सेकम
कीमत पर बेचा जाना
Sold cheaply We bought our house for a song.
Make an ass out of - मूखय वदखनेका
कारण बनना
Cause someone or oneself to look
foolish or stupid
I am not going to go there unprepared and make an ass
of myself.
Beat around the bush - घुमा वफरा कर
बात करना
To treat a topic, but omit its main
points, often intentionally
Will you please stop beating about the bush and get to
the point?
Achilles' heel - कमजोरी A fatal weakness in spite of overall
strength
The corrupt minister is regarded as the government's
Achilles’ heel and is expected to resign.
Gnash your teeth - क्रोवधत होना Express rage The boss will definitely start gnashing his teeth once he
hears about this printing mishap.
Let something slip through one's
fingers - वनरियक प्रर्ास
To waste an opportunity to
achieve something
We had the cell guarded by three people, but still we let
her slip through our fingers somehow.

sections.title: Word series
sections.text:
PANDEMONIUM –
बडा उपद्रि
Wild and noisy disorder or
confusion - ANARCHY
Syn- anarchy, brouhaha, chaos,
ruckus, tumult, uproar,
Ant.- order, quiet, harmony, silence
TEMPORARY –
अथिार्ी
Not lasting or needed for very long -
INTERIM
Syn- transitory, momentary, ephemeral,
fugitive
Ant- lasting, ceaseless, perennial,
irreversible
ASTONISHMENT –
अचंभा
A great surprise - WONDER
Syn- amazement, awe, perplexity,
dismay, bafflement
Ant- anticipation, familiarity,
intimacy, disregard, boredom
ACCURATELY –
सही रूप में
In a way that is correct, exact, and without
any mistakes - EXACTLY
Syn- precisely, unerringly, faultlessly,
reliably, correctly
Ant- carelessly, faultily, clumsily, inaptly
CONDESCENDING –
कृ पालु
Showing or characterized by a
patronizing or superior attitude
toward - PATRONISING
Syn- arrogant, snobbish, egotistic,
imperious, disdainful
Ant- gracious, civil, reverent,
mannerly, obliging
REVIVE –
पुनजीवित
Bring back (a previous right, practice,
custom, or situation) - RESTORE
Syn- rejuvenate, resusciate, regenerate,
renew, revitalize
Ant- abolish, quash, annul, abrogate,
extirpate
ABOMINABLE –
वघनौना
Causing intense displeasure,
disgust, or resentment - AWFUL
Syn- nasty, nauseating, loathsome,
obnoxious, appalling
Ant- pleasing, desirable, alluring,
laudable
RAMIFICATION –
पररणाम
A complex or unwelcome consequence
of an action or event - CONCLUSION
Syn- outcome, result, effect,
consequence
Ant- cause, origin, source, antecedent
BLOATED –
फू ला हुआ
Enlarged beyond normal from
internal pressure - SWOLLEN
Syn- dilated, turgid, varicose,
expanded, inflated
Ant- shrivelled, wrinkly, faded,
compressed
ENDORSE –
समियन
To approve openly - CONFIRM
Syn- advocate, patronise, authorise,
ratify, legislate
Ant- oppose, condemn, censure,
criticise, disapprove

sections.title: Idioms & phrases
sections.text:
Get up on the wrong side of the bed –
चिड़चिड़़ेमूड मेंचिन की शुरुआत होना
Start the day in a bad mood, which
continues all day long
You seem to be in a very bad temper
today. Did you get out on the wrong side
of the bed?
Learn by heart –
चकसी िीज को याि रखना
To memorize something Ask Harsh to recite the poem—he learned
it by heart.
At the drop of a hat –
चिना चकसी ि़ेरी क़े, तुरंत
Without any hesitation; instantly Any time I need help, he's there at the
drop of a hat.
Beat a dead horse – ऐसी िीज पर ऊजााििााि करना
चजसक़े सफल होऩेकी संभावना नहीं
To uselessly dwell on a subject far
beyond its point of resolution
We've all moved on from that problem, so
there's no use beating a dead horse.
Whoop it up – शोर मिाना या शोरगुल स़ेजश्न मनाना Enjoying in a noisy way, usually in a
group
Every spring they whoop it up for the
circus.
With a vengeance – अप़ेक्षा या सामान् य स़ेअचिक मात्रा क़े
साथ
Used to emphasise the degree to
which something occurs
It began to rain again with a vengeance.
Up against the wall – गंभीर मुश्किलोंमें In an inextricable situation Sometimes, the most innovative solutions
come to us when we're up against a wall.
Reap the whirlwind – कायों क़े नकारात्मक पररणामों को
भुगतना
Suffer negative consequences as a
result of one’s actions
If you don't do your homework now, you'll
reap the whirlwind when you have to take
your final exam.
Of the first water – उत्तम गुणवत्ता का Of the best quality The restaurant is renowned for serving
food of the first water.
Weather the storm – कचिन समय स़ेगुजरना Survive a period of difficulty I am sure that Khalid is in the right
situation to weather the storm.
Spin your wheels – अपना समय या प्रयास ििााि करना Waste your time or efforts If we're just spinning our wheels, let us
know and we'll quit.
Wear the green willow – एकतरफा प्यार सहना Suffer unrequited love I wore the green willow after my true love
married another man.
Wild and woolly – चिखऩेया व्यवहार मेंअसभ्य Uncouth in appearance or
behaviour
I’ve seen wild and woolly looks but none
as bad as this one.
Give it a whirl – कु छ नया करऩेकी कोचशश To try out something I don't usually like hot tea, but it's so cold
out that I gave it a whirl today.
Be in the red – कजामेंहोना To be in debt We're back in the red because sales are
way down this quarter.
Come hell or high water – िािा क़े िावजूि पऱेशान न
होना
No matter what I'll get you to the airport by noon, come
hell or high water!
Carry the can – स्वीकार करना To take the responsibility of some
misdemeanour
As usual, I was left to carry the can.
Be a dab hand at something – चकसी काम मेंचवश़ेषज्ञ
या कु शल
Skilled in a particular area Priya is a dab hand at cooking.
Foot the bill – चिल का भुगतान करना To pay for something I don’t want to foot the bill for this stupid
shopping.
A hair’s breadth – िहुत छोटी िू री या मात्रा में Telling about the smallest possible
amount or degree of something
His finger was within a hair's breadth of
touching the alarm

sections.title: Word series
sections.text:
GRADUALLY –
िीऱे- िीऱे
In a gradual way; slowly; by degrees -
STEADILY
Syn. slowly, leisurely, languidly,
torpidly, sluggish
Ant.- abruptly, suddenly, immediately,
hastily, briskly, swift
MANIFEST –
घोषणापत्र
Not subject to misinterpretation or more
than one interpretation – OBVIOUS
Syn.-distinct, divulged, apparent, glaring,
explicit, palpable
Ant.- ambiguous, hidden, enigmatic,
indecipherable, arcane, mysterious,
surreptitious, vague
CRUCIAL –
महत्वपूणा
Extremely important or necessary
- CENTRAL
essential, decisive, momentous,
imperative, critical, vital,
Ant.- inessential, insignificant,
minor, optional, trivial
RELUCTANT –
अचनच्छु क
Feeling or showing hesitation or
unwillingness – UNEAGER
Syn. Unwilling, averse, hesitant, loath,
uncertain,
Ant. - eager, enthusiastic, inclined,
confident, voluntary, willing
EFFICIENCY –
क्षमता
The good use of time and energy in a
way that does not waste any
- PRODUCTIVITY
Syn. ability, Adaptability, capability,
competence, expertise, aptness,
effectiveness
Ant.- inability, inadequacy, ineptitude,
incapability
PERSEVERANCE –
दृढ़ता
Continued effort to do or achieve something
despite difficulties, failure, or opposition –
CERTAINTY
Syn.-determination, endurance, diligence,
tenacity, rigidity, steadiness,
Ant.- reluctance, indolence, indetermination,
fragility, indifference
DEVOUT –
िाचमाक
Having or showing deep religious
feeling or commitment – RIGHTEOUS
MOTIVE – उद्द़ेश्य A reason for doing something – REASON
Syn. aim, intention, purpose, ambition,
impulse
Syn. ardent, fervent, pious, religious,
profound, holy,
Ant.- frigid, fickle, faithless, perfidious,
renegade, dissident
Ant.- hindrance, deterrent, discouragement,
annex, obstruction
ESTIMATE –
आकलन
Evaluate the nature, ability, or q uality
of – ASSESS
Syn. appraisal, rating, opinion,
measure, valuation
ant- ignorance, fact, truth
REGIME – शासन A mode or system of rule or government -
TERRITORY
Syn. administration, establishment,
government, management, reign, rule
ant.- subordination submission
subservience, acquiescence,conformity

sections.title: Idioms & phrases
sections.text:
Jog someone’s memory – किसी िो
िु छ याद कदलानेिे कलए
To cause someone to remember
something
I had no recollection of that vacation until the photo
jogged my memory.
Get cracking – किसी िाययिो शुरू िरना To start doing something Get cracking, or you'll be up all night working on your
book report.
Paper over cracks – समस्या िो कछपाना To hide problems She tried to paper over the cracks, but I could see that the
relationship was failing.
Catch 22 – किशेष स्थिकि किसमेंिोई िीि
नहीींसििा
A particular situation in which one
cannot do anything
David is caught in a Catch-22 situation, unable to choose
which way to go.
Alarums and Excursion – Confused activity and uproar The alarums and excursions in the living room woke me
from a sound sleep.
Up in the air – अभी िि िय न होना Still to be settled Our vacation plans are still up in the air as we keep
differing over our choice of locations.
Give oneself air – कदखािटी होना Pretend to be good Santy should not give herself the airs as she’s no different
from the rest of us.
Alphabet soup – असमींिस िी स्थिकि Incomprehensible or confusing
mix
All of these acronyms in the manual have started to look
like alphabet soup.
Be all one to – िोई अींिर न िरना Make no difference I don't really care what movie we see, it's all one to me.
An article of faith – दृढ़ किश्वास A firmly held belief In prep school, it is taken as an article of faith that
everyone must go on to college.
In the ascendant – सत्ता या प्रभाि मेंिृस्ि Rising in power or influence She is doing quite well in her organisation and is very
much in the ascendant to getting the promotion.
Bring home the bacon – िीकििोपाियन
िरना या पररिार िेकलए पैसा िमाना, अपने
िाम मेसफल होना
Supply material support, to be
victorious
As the head of the family, he ensures that he brings home
the bacon.
Have the ball at your feet – िु छ िरने
िे कलयेसिोत्तम स्थिकि मेंहोना
To be in the best position to do
something
With your grades and extracurriculars, you'll have the ball
at your feet in your college search.
Banana oil – बेिुिी बाि Nonsensical talk Look, I know I won't get past the first round of this
tournament, so you can stop feeding me banana oil.
Hornet’s nest – खिरनाि, िकटल स्थिकि A troublesome situation If we do invade, I fear that we will find ourselves in a real
hornet's nest.
In the teeth of – िे बाििूद In Spite of something In the teeth of the boss's disapproval, we decided to go
forward with the project anyway.
In a flutter – घबराहट िी स्थिकि In a nervous state We were all in a flutter waiting to meet the President at
our school rally.
All Greek to me – समझ सेबाहर Incomprehensible He tried to explain the rules of the game to me, but it was
all Greek to me.
Mealy mouthed –बाि िो टालनेिाला,
खुशामदी िरना
Unwilling to state something He repeated that he did not intend to be mealy-mouthed
with the country's leaders.
No love lost – पसींद न होना Intense dislike There was no love lost between Sam and Dennis. They
could never work together.

sections.title: Word series
sections.text:
GENERIC- व्यापि Shared by, typical of, or relating to a
whole group of similar things, rather
than to any particular thing -
UNIVERSAL
Syn- common, general, wide,
nonexclusive
Ant- exclusive, specific, particular
TRANSMIT –
सींचाररि िरना
To broadcast something, or to send out or
carry signals or messages using radio,
television - CONVEY
Syn- address, broadcast, conduct,
disseminate
Ant.- hold, halt, avoid, dodge
PROMPT - शीघ्र To make something happen: -QUICK
Syn- immediate, instantaneous,
expeditious, brisk, rapid, speedy
Ant.- sluggish, tardy, negligent,
lethargic
NUMEROUS –
अनेि
Consisting of great numbers of units or
individuals - SEVERAL
Syn- plentiful, various, infinite, abundant
Ant.- little, miniature, uniform, tiny
DEDICATED –
समकपयि
To give all of your energy, time￾COMMITTED
Syn- devoted, enthusiastic, faithful,
zealous,
Ant.- disloyal, inconstant, indifferent
CHAOS -
अरािििा, अव्यिथिा
Complete disorder and confusion -
CONFUSION
Syn- anarchy, disarray, discord, turmoil,
tumult
Ant.- harmony, peace, quiet, calm
IOTA - कबींदुमात्र An extremely small amount: - BIT
Syn- ounce, whit, hint, speck
Ant.- lot, exceed
REJUVENATE-
िीर्णोिार िरना
To make someone look or feel young and
energetic again - REFRESH
Syn. refurbish, renew, restore, invigorate,
revitalize,
Ant.- damage, destroy
YIELD (n) –
उपि
To supply or produce something
positive such as a profit, an amount of
food or information -HARVEST
SLACK – सुस्त, ढीला Not tight; loose - CARELESS
Syn. lax, inattentive, lackadaisical, idle,
slothful, tardy, lethargic, slovenly, inert,
indolent, leisurely
Syn. produce, generate, blossom,
accrue, effectuate, furnish
Ant.- lose, deplete, squander,
dissipate, drain
Ant- attentive, conscientious, meticulous,
concerned, alert, painstaking, scrupulous,
studious
DERIDE -
उपहास िरना
To laugh at or insult contemptuously -
MOCK
Syn. Syn- disdain, disparage, ridicule,
gibe, jeer, scoff,
Ant.- admire, approve, compliment,
praise
PRINCIPLE –
कसिाींि
A basic truth or theory : an idea that forms
the basis of something -AXIOM
Syn- assumption, basis, doctrine, canon,
precept, ethic
Ant,- ambiguity, effect, end
POIGNANT -
माकमयि, िटु
Causing a strong feeling of sadness -
TOUCHING
Syn- emotional, disturbing, pathetic,
sentimental, intense
Ant,- cheerful, indifferent, soothing,
pleasant
COMMENCE -
आरींभ िरना
To begin -START
Syn. Syn- begin, inaugurate, initiate, arise,
originate
Ant.- complete, conclude, finish
CALM - शाींि A quiet and peaceful state or condition
- RELAXED
Syn. Syn- mild, placid, serene, smooth,
pacific,
Ant.- agitated, harsh, violent, furious
BREAKTHROUGH - A person's first important success -
DISCOVERY
Syn- boost, hike, leap. Progress,
Ant.,- decline, decrease, loss
TAG (n) - To provide or mark with - LABEL
Syn- badge, card, sticker, stamp, logo
SPILL - किरािट To (cause to) flow, move, fall, or spread
over the edge or outside the limits of
something-DROP
Syn- discharge, dribble, pour, spray,
squirt, scatter
Ant.- collect, gather

sections.title: Idioms & phrases
sections.text:
Out of sorts (बीमार महसूस करना) To be unwell The baby is out of sorts. Maybe she's getting a new tooth.
Pay lip service- (बनावटी हमददी ददखाना,
ददखावा करना)
Pretend to regard I'm tired of politicians who do nothing but pay lip service to
the major issues affecting our country.
Rip up old sores- (पुराना झगडा दिर शुरू
करना)
To revive forgotten
quarrel
They rip up old sores just for a pen.
Rule the roost – (मुखखया होना) To dominate You just need to accept that your daughter is going to rule the
roost for most of her childhood.
As fit as a fiddle- (स्वस्थ्य होना) Strong and healthy After a refreshing vacation by the sea, I now feel fit as a fiddle.
Argus eyed- (चौकन्ना होना) Observant Servants are argus-eyed and uncharitable in their conclusions.
To bid defiance- (अवहेलना करना) To disregard recklessly With every expression of hate and scorn rising to her face, she
bids him defiance.
With bated breath-
(घबराहट में, दचिंता में)
In anxiety The exhausted attendants stood about the bed with bated
breath.
To clip one’s wings-
(दकसी की आजादी को प्रदतबिंदित करना)
To restrict someone’s
freedom
The boss is always trying to clip my wings.
Cloven hoof- (बुरी मिंशा) The evil intention I played with her, but her young keenness detected the cloven
hoof of duty.
Draconian law – (अत्यन्त कदिन दनयम) Extremely severe law These ancient laws form a somewhat Draconian law.
To fall flat- (कोई प्रभाव न पड़ना) To have no effect Our proposals were likely to fall flat.
To gird up the loins- (कदिन मेहनत के दलये
तैयार होना)
To prepare for hard
work
I am girding up my lions for that crucial interview.
High and mighty- (घमिंडी) Arrogant Don’t get high and mighty with me.
To get more kicks than half pence- (प्रशिंसा
सेज्यादा दतरस्कार होना)
Harsh treatment than
rewards
As a cabbie on these streets, you're greeted with more kicks
than half pence at this hour of the night.
All over hell’s half acre (हर जगह) Everywhere There are thunderstorms popping up all over Hell’s half acre.
Dust and ashes –
(दनराशाजनक)
Something that is very
disappointing
The party would be dust and ashes if he couldn’t come.
The ayes have it-
(सबकी सहमदत होना)
The affirmative votes
are in the majority
Few were sure whether this controversial tax bill would be
passed, but it looks like the ayes have it.
Play one’s ace-
(सबसेबद़िया हदियार इस्तेमाल करना)
To use one’s best
weapon of resource
It’s time to play our ace and put our strongest player back on
the field.
Be full of beans-
(उत्साह, जोश सेभरा हुआ)
Full of energy and life Jem was full of beans after a long sleep.

sections.title: Word series
sections.text:
ADJUST -
समायोदजत करना,
अनुकू दलत करना
To change something slightly, especially to
make it more correct, effective, or suitable￾ADAPT
Syn.-conform, accommodate, alter,
organize
Ant.- disarrange, disperse, scatter,
dishevel, unsettle, entangle
GRUMBLE
दशकायत करना
To complain about someone or
something in an annoyed way - GROAN
Syn.- moan, squawk, complain, grouse,
gripe, inveigh,
Ant- Praise, compliment, plaudit,
delight, appreciate, favor, surrender
TERMINATION –
समाखि
The act of ending something or the end of
something - CONCLUSION
Syn. discontinuation, cessation, abortion,
expiry, finale,
Ant.- continuance, inauguration, initiation
WANDER- इिर-उिर
घूमना
To walk around slowly in a relaxed way
or without any clear purpose or direction
- ROAM
Syn. Syn- amble, cruise, drift, meander,
ramble, roam, straggle, stroll
MUNCH – चबड़-
चबड़ करके खाना
To eat something, especially noisily -CHEW
Syn- bite, grind, crunch, crush, masticate
ABOLISH￾समाप्त करना
To end an activity or custom officially -
ELIMINATE
Syn- abrogate, annul, eradicate,
terminate, nullify, annihilate
Ant.- allow, establish, permit, commence
DEBILITATE￾कमजोर कर देना
To make someone or something physically
weak - WEAKEN
Syn- attenuate, cripple, disable, enervate,
extenuate
Ant.- strengthen, cure, assuage, invigorate
TESTIFY- गवाही या
साक्ष्य देना
To speak seriously about something,
especially in a law court, or to give or
provide proof - AFFIRM
Syn- announce, swear, attest, certify,
depose, declare
Ant.- conceal, hide, contradict, refute
CELEBRATE￾समारोह करना,
उत्सव मनाना
To take part in special enjoyable activities
in order to show that a particular occasion
is important - HONOUR
Syn- laud, achievement, perform, feast
Ant.- blame, reproach, denounce,
condemn
BRAT- ढीि बच्चा A child, especially one who behaves
badly - SPOILT CHILD
Syn- punk, rascal, urchin, youngster
Ant.- angel
ABSOLVE- दोषमुक्त
करना
To set (someone) free from an obligation
or the consequences of guilt -PARDON
Syn- acquit, exempt, exonerate, loose,
relieve
LEVERAGE लाभ लेना Influence or power used to achieve a
desired result - INFLUENCE
Syn- advantage, clout, grease, power
Ant,- weakness
Ant.- accuse, blame, censure, condemn,
convict
BANG – पीटना,
जोरदार दस्तक
To knock, hit, or thrust vigorously often
with a sharp noise - BEAT
Syn- bump, smack, punch, cuff, collide
INTEGRATE -
एकीकृ त करना
To form, coordinate, or blend into a
functioning or unified whole -
ASSIMILATE
Syn- combine, conform, merge, blend,
combine
Ant,- disarrange, disconnect, disperse,
separate
PONDER￾दवचार करना
To think about - MEDITATE
Syn- consider, evaluate, examine, think,
wonder,
Ant.- discard, disregard, neglect, forget
ABSTAIN - बचना To choose not to do or have something
- REFRAIN
Syn- cease, forgo, evade, avoid,
abnegate,
Ant.- embrace, involve, partake
SHIMMER--
दटमदटमाना
To shine with a soft tremulous or fitful
light - SHINE
Syn- glimmer, blinking, scintillation,
sparkle, twinkle, gleam
Ant.- darkness, dullness, dim, murkiness,
gloom
CADENCE - ताल A regular beat or rhythm – RHYTHM
Syn- accent, intonation, modulation,
pitch
UNCANNY￾रहस्यमय
Strange or unusual in a way that is
surprising or difficult to understand -
MYSTERIOUS
Syn- astonishing, astounding, exceptional,
weird, enigmatic, strange, peculiar,
Ant.- ordinary, common, normal,
mundane, conventional
HUMDRUM - नीरस Lacking variety -BORING
Syn- dreary, monotonous, mundane,
dull, tedious,
Ant.- exciting, interesting, abnormal,
different, exceptional, extraordinary,
lively
